players.product: Enhanced geothermal (EGS) 24/7 baseload power from modular GeoBlocks (Cape Station geocluster, Utah) under long-term PPAs with hyperscalers, utilities and industrial buyers, grid-connected and behind-the-meter

quarterly_data.signal: Fervo's Q1 2026 earnings release (8-K): Q1 2026 capital expenditures of $172.8 million versus $105.4 million in Q1 2025; it expected total capital expenditures of approximately $1.2 billion from Q2 2026 through Q1 2027, primarily for Cape Station Phase I and Phase II construction and other GeoClusters. Q1 2026 operating loss $20.1 million and net loss $31.8 million. Cape Station Phase II (approximately 400 megawatts, eight 50-megawatt GeoBlocks) commenced construction in Q1 2026 with all long-lead equipment secured, two Helmerich & Payne rigs drilling and all four initial Fervo Generation 3.0 wells drilled on the first pad. At Blanford, Utah, the Cottonwood observation well reached 555 degrees F at 11,200 feet, the hottest well in Fervo's history.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 capex $172.8 million (vs $105.4 million); ~$1.2 billion capex Q2 2026-Q1 2027; Phase II ~400 MW, all long-lead equipment secured

quarterly_data.signal: Fervo's Q1 2026 earnings release (8-K) on supply chain: in the first half of 2026 it signed strategic partnerships with three key suppliers, Turboden, ABB and Vallourec, spanning power generation, electrical equipment and well construction; the five-year supply agreement with Vallourec is expected to provide a sufficient base of domestically-manufactured tubulars for scaled subsurface development.

connects_to.relationship: enhanced geothermal power offtake (Geothermal Framework Agreement and power purchase agreements)

contracts.signal: Fervo's Q1 2026 earnings release (8-K): in March 2026 Fervo executed a Geothermal Framework Agreement (GFA) with Google establishing a development framework for up to 3 gigawatts of geothermal capacity through 2033, including 1 gigawatt of proposed projects in the first two years, streamlining future offtake through a defined contract structure and priority geographies. CEO Tim Latimer cited '658 megawatts of contracted power purchase agreements and a 3- gigawatt geothermal framework agreement with Google'.
contracts.units: up to 3 gigawatts through 2033 (1 gigawatt of proposed projects in the first two years)

connects_to.relationship: Organic Rankine Cycle turbine supply through subsidiary Turboden

contracts.signal: Fervo's Q1 2026 earnings release (8-K): Fervo and Turboden, a subsidiary of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, entered a turbine supply agreement covering up to 35 Organic Rankine Cycle units that together represent 1,750 megawatts of total power capacity.
contracts.units: up to 35 Organic Rankine Cycle units (1,750 megawatts)

connects_to.relationship: motor control and electrification solutions for Cape Station

contracts.signal: Fervo's Q1 2026 earnings release (8-K): Fervo entered into a strategic agreement with ABB to provide advanced motor control and electrification solutions for Cape Station, expected to help mitigate long lead-time risks that competing energy technologies increasingly confront.
